result.question: Why did the four men with leprosy go to the camp of the Arameans?

readings.answer: To try to live, since the Arameans might spare them.
readings.support: If they let us live, we will live

readings.answer: Because every other option meant death (in the famine-stricken city or by sitting there).
readings.support: we will die there from the famine in the city; but if we sit here, we will also die

assessments.reason: It captures the motive that the Arameans might let them live, which the passage states (“If they let us live, we will live”), though it omits the contrast that staying or entering the city meant certain death.

It reflects the stated alternatives of certain death by staying or entering the famine-stricken city (“we will die there… if we sit here, we will also die”), though it omits the expressed hope that the Arameans might spare them.
